text: The Patriots enter Sunday's Week 5 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders as a team simultaneously celebrating its storied past while navigating a present beset by injuries—Adam Vinatieri will be honored during halftime as the newest Pro Football Hall of Fame inductee, with Robert Kraft drawing parallels between this squad and the 2001 championship team on the 25th anniversary of that first title, even as the team deals with significant roster attrition heading into kickoff at 1 PM ET. The injury situation is particularly acute in the secondary, where starting cornerbacks Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis will both be unavailable, forcing the Patriots to rely on newly signed practice-squad call-up Kindle Vildor, while at skill positions, veteran wide receiver Mack Hollins was placed on injured reserve with a calf injury Saturday, and fullback Reggie Gilliam also landed on IR, though special-teams ace Brenden Schooler was activated to the 53-man roster in the flurry of moves. The Patriots will don throwback uniforms for the contest—a nice nostalgic touch given the Hall of Fame honor and anniversary recognition—as they prepare to face Raiders quarterback Kirk Cousins, whose hot start to the season has been one of the NFL's biggest surprises.
